meta.title: Philosophy — Erveca Studio
meta.desc: The philosophy of Erveca Studio: videogames made from and for rural areas, with the culture, craftsmanship and landscape of La Rioja as a starting point.
philosophy.label: Our philosophy
philosophy.title: Videogames that stay in the village
philosophy.lead: Erveca Studio was born in Pradillo, a village of just over sixty inhabitants in the Cameros mountains of La Rioja. We believe rural life is not a backdrop: it is the origin, the content and the destination of everything we do.
philosophy.v1.title: Playing to fight depopulation
philosophy.v1.desc: Our starting point is to fight rural depopulation through videogames, showing that quality digital culture can be made from a mountain village, not in spite of it.
philosophy.v2.title: Craftsmanship as game material
philosophy.v2.desc: The almazuelas in Almazuela Picross are not decoration: they are real pieces lent by artisans from the Almazuela Festival of Pradillo. We bring this textile heritage into a digital format accessible from anywhere in the world.
philosophy.v3.title: Made with the people around us
philosophy.v3.desc: Every project brings in local collaborations: music, translation, illustration. Erveca Studio grows as a network of local trades, not as an isolated factory.
philosophy.quote: “We decided to take all the almazuelas that were in the tourist office, talk to the artisans and even ask for a few more so we could show them.”
philosophy.loom.alt: Traditional almazuela made by artisans from Pradillo
philosophy.loom.label: From the loom to the screen
philosophy.loom.title: Every pixel has roots
philosophy.loom.p1: Almazuelas are traditional textile pieces from La Rioja, made of fabric scraps joined together to form geometric compositions, similar to patchwork. Their name comes from the Arabic almusálla, "prayer rug", and for generations they have been used as bedspreads, cushions and wall hangings.
philosophy.loom.p2: In Almazuela Picross, solving each nonogram unlocks a real fabric scrap, and when you complete the level those scraps are assembled into a full almazuela. The method also values making the most of materials and sustainability: nothing is wasted, neither on the loom nor in the code.
philosophy.goddess.alt: Bench in Pradillo with an advertisement for the Viuda de Solano candy company
philosophy.goddess.p1: In Goddess of the Skies, our upcoming title, we did not want to cut ourselves off from our rural roots, so we have replaced the fabric scraps with tiles. You will have to look for fragments on different islands and then restore them, just as was done in Pradillo in 2023.
philosophy.goddess.p2: We work at a gentle pace, with no time pressure or anxiety-inducing mechanics. We want playing one of our titles to feel like sitting by the fire listening to a story from the village: calm, close and with something true behind it.
philosophy.next.label: Looking ahead
philosophy.next.title: From Cameros to the world
philosophy.next.p1: Erveca, our flagship project, travels through real villages of the area —Pradillo, Ortigosa, Villoslada— with a magical, medieval air, designed to reconnect new generations with rural life through videogames.
philosophy.next.p2: Almazuela Picross started out as one of Erveca's minigames and has grown into an independent title with an identity of its own, available on Steam and Google Play. Two games, one shared root.
